schema.file: core/memory/schema.ts:25 (MEMORY_SCHEMA, the 9 core tables); plus core/memory/vectors.ts:18 (chunks), core/memory/ingest-lock.ts:58 (ingest_lock), core/memory/consolidator.ts:261 (consolidation_runs), core/scheduler/firelog.ts:27 (proactive_fires) — 14 tables total, 5 schema sources

tables.name: episodes
columns: connector TEXT NOT NULL — surface that produced it (telegram, vault, cli, ...)
thread_key TEXT NOT NULL — session/conversation id within the connector
actor_id INTEGER REFERENCES identities(id) — who produced it, beyond role; ALWAYS NULL in production, see gaps
role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('user','agent','tool','system')
kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('message','tool_result','document','web','media')
vault_path TEXT — nullable, set for vault-sourced episodes
media_meta TEXT — nullable JSON (hash/tier/chunk-index for vault docs)
trust_tier INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND 3
extraction_v INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 — pipeline version that last processed this row
superseded_at TEXT — nullable; retires the text (e.g. vault file changed) without deleting the row
tables.rowsMeaning: one append-only record of something said, uploaded or replied — the only source of truth in the whole store; a row is a record that something happened, never itself a belief.
constraints: CHECK kind IN ('message','tool_result','document','web','media') — the 5 real values

tables.name: episodes_fts
columns: content — FTS5 virtual table, external-content over episodes(content), content_rowid='id'
tables.rowsMeaning: full-text shadow of episodes.content, kept in sync by AFTER INSERT/AFTER DELETE triggers (schema.ts:57-62); episodes are append-only so no UPDATE trigger exists or is needed.
constraints: mirrors episodes 1:1 by rowid; never written directly, only via the two triggers

tables.name: entities
columns: kind TEXT NOT NULL — free vocabulary from extraction (person/place/organization/project/concept/event/thing), not CHECK-constrained here
summary TEXT — nullable; declared but NEVER WRITTEN, see gaps
expired_at TEXT — nullable; declared but NEVER WRITTEN (ADR-0040), see notBuilt
tables.rowsMeaning: one node the owner's life is about — a person, place, org, project, etc. — resolved by exact case-insensitive name match within a tenant (store.ts:228-238), never auto-merged across a name mismatch.

tables.name: identities
columns: entity_id INTEGER REFERENCES entities(id) — nullable until linked
link_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unlinked' CHECK IN ('unlinked','proposed','confirmed')
link_evidence INTEGER REFERENCES episodes(id) — required by invariant once confirmed
tables.rowsMeaning: one connector-account (a Telegram user id, etc.) that may or may not yet be linked to an entity — 'one person seen from two connectors is two identities until someone confirms otherwise' (schema.ts:76-77). Has ZERO production writers; see gaps.

tables.name: facts
columns: subject_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES entities(id)
predicate TEXT NOT NULL — free vocabulary, snake_case, canonicalised at extraction
object_id INTEGER REFERENCES entities(id) — nullable, XOR with object_value
object_value TEXT — nullable, XOR with object_id
valid_from TEXT — world-time start; NULL means nobody stated when
valid_to TEXT — world-time end; in production only ever written by supersede(), see gaps
recorded_at TEXT NOT NULL — system-time: when Muffin learned it
expired_at TEXT — system-time: when Muffin stopped believing it; NULL while active
episode_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES episodes(id) — provenance, the field 'why' is built on
speaker_id INTEGER REFERENCES identities(id) — who asserted it; ALWAYS NULL in production, see gaps
trust_tier INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND 3 — inherited from the episode, never higher (invariant trust_tier_raised)
confidence REAL NOT NULL — model confidence at extraction, floor 0.4, never decayed (ADR-0040)
origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'said' CHECK IN ('said','inferred','imported') — only 'said' is produced today
importance INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND 2 — forced-choice at extraction (0 routine/1 notable/2 charged)
superseded_by INTEGER REFERENCES facts(id) — nullable, chains to the fact that replaced this one
tables.rowsMeaning: one belief: subject-predicate-object, set-valued by default (a subject/predicate pair may legally have several simultaneously active facts), bi-temporal, every row self-describing its own provenance and trust — never deleted, only superseded.
constraints: CHECK (object_id IS NULL) <> (object_value IS NULL) — exactly one of the two is set

tables.name: memory_review
columns: kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('contradiction','error')
detail TEXT NOT NULL — judge reasoning, or the error message, verbatim
tables.rowsMeaning: one thing the pipeline would not decide by itself: a judge 'review' verdict (two facts that might conflict) or a pipeline error (failed extraction, unreachable judge, dead embedder). Deliberately has NO status/resolved_at column — 'open' is derived by joining to facts.expired_at (store.ts:116-120), never stored.
constraints: explicitly NOT part of the droppable/reconstructible derived plane (schema.ts:130-136)

tables.name: profiles
tables.rowsMeaning: designed to hold a generated summary of one entity. ZERO writers and ZERO readers anywhere in the codebase — schema only, see notBuilt/gaps.
constraints: PK is entity_id itself (one profile per entity)

tables.name: digests
tables.rowsMeaning: designed to hold a generated summary over a time window/scope (a 'dream'/compaction pass). ZERO writers and ZERO readers anywhere in the codebase — schema only, see notBuilt/gaps.

tables.name: functional_predicates
tables.rowsMeaning: the small, owner-visible allowlist of predicates that must hold exactly one current value per subject (date_of_birth, place_of_birth, legal_name, tax_id — schema.ts:178-183); everything else is a set by default.
constraints: PK predicate; seeded with 4 defaults on every MemoryStore construction via INSERT OR IGNORE (store.ts:147-150)

tables.name: chunks
columns: source_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('episode','fact')
text TEXT NOT NULL — exact text that was embedded
embedding_v TEXT NOT NULL — embedder id string, doubles as a version tag
tables.rowsMeaning: one embedded chunk of episode or fact text, metadata side of the vector index; text+id live here, the float vector lives in chunks_vec at the same rowid. Defined in core/memory/vectors.ts, not in schema.ts's MEMORY_SCHEMA.
constraints: UNIQUE(tenant_id,source_kind,source_id,embedding_v) — changing embedder makes the whole corpus pending again rather than mixing dimensions

tables.name: chunks_vec
columns: rowid — = chunks.id, must be inserted as BigInt (vec0 rejects plain Number)
tenant_id TEXT PARTITION KEY — moves the tenant filter inside the ANN index itself
embedding float[dimensions] — dimensions from the configured embedder (1024 for the Ollama default)
tables.rowsMeaning: sqlite-vec vec0 virtual table, the actual float vectors. Partitioned by tenant_id since vectors.ts:43-50 so k-nearest-neighbours means 'k of this tenant', not 'k globally, some of which happen to be this tenant's'.
constraints: vec0 virtual table; a migration (vectors.ts:67-104) moves an older unpartitioned layout to this one, preserving vectors rather than re-embedding

tables.name: ingest_lock
columns: id INTEGER PK CHECK (id = 1) — singleton row
tables.rowsMeaning: the one-extractor-at-a-time mutex across processes (a gateway and a REPL window can share one database). BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim, refusal not blocking; stale after 30 minutes regardless of pid liveness.

tables.name: consolidation_runs
columns: merged INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 — duplicates retired by the sweep that run
tables.rowsMeaning: one row per consolidation batch, run or refused — the durable receipt that the lane exists and is or is not working; the only way to tell a legitimately-quiet lane (0 facts, correct on a slow week) from a lane that never starts (also 0 facts).
constraints: rows never deleted (invariant I-8); read by muffin memory stats / muffin doctor

tables.name: proactive_fires
columns: anchor TEXT PK — stable id of the concrete signal, e.g. 'absence:<entityId>:<lastSeen>'
effect TEXT NOT NULL — in practice always 'allow' (the only writer, recordFired, never records defer/deny)
reason TEXT NOT NULL — the evidence, e.g. 'p 0.0231 · 42.0g di silenzio · 5 occasioni'
tables.rowsMeaning: dedup ledger for proactive messages actually delivered, so the same silence is never re-noticed after a restart. Lives in core/scheduler/firelog.ts, not core/memory — included here because it is the durable half of the memory-derived 'gone quiet' signal (core/memory/absence.ts).
constraints: PK anchor; INSERT OR IGNORE so two racing writers keep whichever fired first; rows never deleted (invariant I-8)

planes.name: evidence
planes.what: the append-only record of everything said, uploaded, or replied. The only plane that is never reconstructed from anything else — it is the anything else.
writtenBy: agent/loop.ts:273-282 (user message, written before the model is called)
agent/loop.ts:528-539 (agent's own reply, written after answering)
core/vault/vault.ts:238-259 (vault document chunks, kind:'document', trust tier follows content hash not path)
agent/observe-run.ts:104-115 (proactive 'gone quiet' message, written only after delivery succeeds)
readBy: core/memory/store.ts:637-677 (searchEpisodes — FTS half of recall, now with an EpisodeFilter: includeSuperseded/surface/since/until — the (surface, date_range) primitive of `02-ontologia.md` §9)
core/memory/store.ts:610-624 (episodeWindow — connector/threadKey/createdAt for one episode; read by the vector half's surface filter and by episodeNeighbourhood)
core/memory/store.ts:700-731 (episodeNeighbourhood — the K episodes before/after one episode in its own (connector,thread_key); the `vicinato` primitive of `02-ontologia.md` §9)

planes.name: graph
planes.what: entities, connector identities, and the bi-temporal, set-valued, fully-provenanced facts about them. Architecturally described as reconstructible by replaying episodes through extraction (schema.ts:9-11), but no such replay/rebuild command actually exists in the CLI (cli/memory.ts:27-34 lists why|search|extract|review|stats|check, nothing that clears and re-derives the graph) — bumping EXTRACTION_VERSION only re-queues episodes into the same accumulate-and-reconcile path, it does not wipe and rebuild.
writtenBy: core/memory/ingest.ts:323-345 (addFact, the insert half of reconcile)
cli/memory.ts:326 (resolveContradiction -> supersede — the one owner-driven, non-pipeline write)
readBy: core/memory/recall.ts:428-472 (one-hop graph expansion — one of THREE selectors runs per entity, chosen by `asOf`: activeFacts (now, the default), allFacts (`asOf: 'all'`, what `--history` resolves to), or factsAsOf (a specific instant) — never a fourth query, `asOf` only removes which constant the existing shape uses)

core/memory/store.ts:503-545 (factsAsOf — the graph as it stood at one instant; a fact matches on its belief window OR a *stated* world-time bound, never an inferred one) and core/memory/store.ts:572-598 (nearestFactTo — read only when factsAsOf comes back empty for a matched entity, so a temporal question outside the graph's coverage becomes a named gap instead of silence)
core/memory/absence.ts:214-225 (mention rhythm for the 'gone quiet' signal, tier<=1 only)
core/memory/invariants.ts (7 of 10 property checks touch facts/entities/identities directly)

core/memory/recall.ts:441-467 (the vector half's semantic match on fact text also reads the full row, via factById rather than a second provenance query — the fix for a fact that stayed semantically findable and unmarked after being retired; see gaps/lessons)

planes.name: derived
planes.what: everything meant to be disposable and regenerable from evidence+graph. In practice this plane is two-thirds inert: functional_predicates and the chunks/chunks_vec vector index are real and wired in; profiles and digests (the 'dream'/compaction layer) are schema with nothing on either end.
writtenBy: core/memory/store.ts:147-150 (functional_predicates, seed-only, 4 defaults, every MemoryStore construction)
NONE for profiles or digests — zero writers anywhere in the repo
readBy: core/memory/invariants.ts:110-118 (functional_predicates, via a direct SQL join — NOT via the isFunctional() method, which has zero production callers, see gaps)
NONE for profiles or digests — zero readers anywhere in the repo

writePath.what: Incoming message written as an episode (role:user, trust_tier from principal.kind: 0 owner / 2 group member) before the model is called at all, so a crash mid-turn cannot lose the input that caused it.
The agent's own reply written as a separate episode (role:agent, trust_tier:0) once the turn actually answers.

Turn end calls Consolidator.notify(tenant); silently refused for any tenant other than 'host' (consolidator.ts:519, CONSOLIDATION_TENANT — the group-persona non-profiling guarantee lives here); (re)arms a 20s idle timer, or fires immediately once 12 turns have passed without a qualifying pause (the ceiling backstop).

ingestPending() takes the durable ingest_lock (one extractor at a time, across processes); on success reads up to `limit` pending episodes oldest-first (store.ts:179-190, extraction_v < EXTRACTION_VERSION).

Empty-content, role:'agent', and kind:'document' episodes are marked processed without extraction and without a model call — agent output is 68% of the migrated corpus and mining it would let Muffin manufacture its own facts about the owner; documents are recalled but never mined for beliefs.

One light-model call per remaining episode. Facts under confidence 0.4 are dropped (extract.ts:176); predicates canonicalised to snake_case (extract.ts:186-194); importance derived from two forced-choice booleans, never a 1-10 rating (extract.ts:67-71).
Subject entity resolved by exact case-insensitive name match or created; kind is whatever the first mention guessed and is never overwritten by a later, differently-guessed mention.

Incoming fact compared only against the CURRENT (most-recently-recorded) active belief for that (subject,predicate): none active -> insert free; identical to the current one -> skip free; otherwise -> judge.

One light-model call; reasoning is declared before the verdict in the response schema (the documented fix for a measured judge-collapse bug elsewhere). Verdicts: coexist (default, most common) / supersede / temporal_scope / review. A `supersede` under confidence 0.75 (SUPERSEDE_THRESHOLD, judge.ts:44) is downgraded to review; an unreachable/broken judge is treated the same way, logged, never silently 'added'.

supersede/temporal_scope -> store.supersede() (closes valid_to only for temporal_scope, when the judge stated one); review -> both facts stay active, a memory_review row is recorded; coexist -> both stay, nothing further happens.
extraction_v is advanced for that one episode immediately after its own facts+judge calls finish (not at end of batch), so a crash mid-batch replays at most one episode next run.
After the loop, any episode/fact text not yet embedded for the current embedder id is embedded and written to chunks/chunks_vec; failures here are retried next run, never lost.

Only if the batch added >=1 fact: exact-normalised-string duplicates among currently-active beliefs for the same (subject,predicate,object) are retired to the newest row, via supersede() with valid_to forced to NULL (a duplicate never represents a real world-time boundary).

One consolidation_runs row per fire (ran, budget, busy, or error) — durable, never deleted; the only way `muffin memory stats`/`muffin doctor` can tell a legitimately-quiet lane from one that never runs.

recallPath.file: agent/loop.ts:289-298 (automatic, pre-loop) and agent/tools/memory.ts:112-214 (memory_search tool, on-demand mid-turn)
recallPath.what: Every turn's own text is recalled automatically before the model sees anything; the model may also call memory_search for a second, purposeful query it could not have anticipated at turn start — the only path that can set asOf/history/surface/since/until/around, since the automatic recall never asks a temporal question. Both paths call core/memory/recall.ts:369 recall(), tenant fixed by the caller, never by the argument list.
recallPath.note: memory_search has no tenant parameter at all, by design (agent/tools/memory.ts:22-24) — no prompt can widen its own scope.

recallPath.stage: temporal instant resolved at the boundary
recallPath.file: core/memory/recall.ts:108-138 (normaliseDate) and :166-180 (checkTemporalWindow), called from cli/main.ts:505-517 and agent/tools/memory.ts:145-177 before recall() is ever reached
recallPath.what: A raw string (YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD) becomes an ISO instant, or is refused outright — a date SQLite cannot compare would otherwise turn every temporal predicate false, and an empty result reads as amnesia rather than as a typo. checkTemporalWindow then refuses two further cases before anything opens: since after until (a window that cannot contain anything) and an asOf that has not happened yet — both shared by the CLI and the tool so the two boundaries cannot drift, and both exempt `EVERY_INSTANT` ('all', what --history resolves to) from the future check, since it sorts after any ISO date lexicographically ('a' > '2').
recallPath.note: asOf is one parameter with three states — absent (now), an instant, or 'all' (every instant) — not a boolean beside a date. RecallOptions.includeHistory (a second boolean) was removed; `knowledge/05-person-model.md` names exactly this two-knobs-for-one-idea shape as the antipattern.

recallPath.what: FTS5 (unicode61, diacritics stripped) over episodes.content, tenant-scoped, limit*2 candidates, SQLite's own bm25-derived `rank`. Superseded episodes are excluded UNLESS asOf is set (includeSuperseded), and surface/since/until narrow the SQL WHERE directly — the (surface, date_range) primitive of `02-ontologia.md` §9.
recallPath.note: Exact words; finds the literal term, misses the paraphrase.

recallPath.what: k-NN (k=limit*2) within the tenant's own chunks_vec partition (partition key, not a post-filter — vectors.ts:43-50 describes the bug this fixed: a post-filter let a talkative tenant push another tenant's hits out of the k window entirely). A fact hit is read through factById (store.ts:935) rather than a narrower provenance query, so it gets the exact same expired/validFrom/validTo/replacedBy labelling as the graph hop, via the shared successorOf helper (recall.ts:655), and is dropped entirely if retired and includeSuperseded is not set. An episode hit reads connector/supersededAt from provenanceOf (store.ts:903-932) and is dropped if it fails the retirement gate or the surface/since/until filter — the same guarantees the text half enforces in SQL, enforced here in application code because the vector index has no notion of either.
recallPath.note: Paraphrase; drifts on names/dates/codes. Degrades to text-only (skips this half, appends 'vector-non-disponibile(...)' to strategies) rather than failing the turn if the embedder is down. Nothing re-embeds a fact or episode on retirement, so its old text stays semantically findable forever — which is exactly why this half needed its own gate rather than inheriting the text half's; see gaps and docs/lessons.md.

recallPath.what: Capitalised words in the query (recall.ts:750, extractCandidateNames, deliberately crude — a wrong guess only costs an empty lookup) are looked up as entity names (entitiesByName, store.ts:740). Per matched entity, ONE of three selectors runs, chosen by asOf and nothing else: activeFacts (asOf absent — now), allFacts (asOf:'all' — what --history resolves to), or factsAsOf (asOf a specific instant — store.ts:503-545, the graph as it stood then: a fact matches on its belief window [recorded_at, expired_at) OR a *stated* world-time bound, an unknown bound never excludes but never invents a date either). Results are bounded by selectForExpansion before being fused.
recallPath.note: One hop only, by measurement: widening graph expansion on a comparable system cost 44 points on a benchmark (recall.ts:17-19).

recallPath.stage: the gap — a temporal question the graph cannot answer
recallPath.what: When factsAsOf comes back empty for an entity the text/graph match already found, that is not silence: nearestFactTo finds the closest thing on record by recorded_at, and a RecallGap is appended to RecallResult.gaps naming the entity, the instant asked for, and the nearest belief if one exists. This is the failure this primitive exists to prevent: asked 'who was my contact in May' about an entity whose graph starts in June, recall used to return June's belief with no mark on it — a wrong answer that looks like an answer.
recallPath.note: Never a classifier: nothing inspects the query text for 'in May'. The caller (model or CLI flag) states the instant; recall only says what it could and could not find at it — `02-ontologia.md` §9 forbids an 'is this a historical question' classifier by name.

recallPath.what: At most 6 of an entity's facts reach the fusion: the 6 most recent, plus — if a more-important fact was cut and it beats the weakest of the 6 kept — one swap. Order is always by recency after the swap; importance decided ONLY whether a fact got a seat, never its position.

Every hit from all three halves — text, vector, graph — is scored 1/(60+rank+1) using its rank *within its own half's list*, and summed by a (kind,id) key across halves; the merged map is sorted descending; the turn's own just-recorded input episode is excluded (excludeEpisodeId).
recallPath.note: WHAT FUSES: text-rank, vector-rank, graph-expansion-rank, all through the identical formula, no per-source weight or multiplier. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT A SIGNAL: importance never enters this formula — recall.ts:302-321 gives the exact number, promoting a fact from last slot to first in the graph expansion is worth 0.001242 in RRF space, 73% of the threshold at which the field's own research says a fused list silently becomes 'sorted by importance, tie-broken by relevance'. An earlier version DID order the graph expansion by importance and that was the bug being fixed. trust_tier and confidence are likewise absent from the score itself — both only ever affect display/labelling and the turn's inherited taint (recallTaint), never rank.

recallPath.what: Only when >= RERANK_MIN_CANDIDATES (12) fused candidates exist: one light-model call reorders the top limit*5 by relevance to the query text; anything the model dropped or an unparseable response leaves out is still appended as a tail rather than lost.
recallPath.note: Silently degrades to the RRF order on any provider failure or unparseable response (rerank.ts:64-92) — but recall.ts:588 unconditionally labels the strategy 'rerank(<id>)' once this branch is entered, so a failed rerank is indistinguishable, from the `strategies` field alone, from a successful one. Contrast the vector half, which explicitly reports its own failure (recall.ts:503). See gaps.

recallPath.stage: the neighbourhood — attached after the cut, never inside it
recallPath.what: When options.neighbours (`around` on the tool) is set, each kept episode item gets up to MAX_NEIGHBOURS=5 (recall.ts:293) episodes before and after it, from its own (connector, thread_key) only — the `vicinato` primitive of `02-ontologia.md` §9. Appended to the survivors with score:0 and neighbourOf:<anchorId> rather than fused: a neighbour did not match the query and must not take a slot from, or change the rank of, something that did.
recallPath.note: Taint rule: each neighbour carries its OWN trust_tier, so recallTaint's max-over-items already raises the turn to a group neighbour's tier — collapsing the window into the anchor's tier would have been the hole. The count is clamped at the primitive, not only described as small in a comment: options.neighbours is a tool argument the model controls.

recallPath.what: Sliced to `limit` (default 8, recall.ts:375). Each item rendered as '[source, temporal-label, origin-mark, intorno-mark] text', a superseded fact's line followed by '↳ sostituito da: <successor text>' on its own line, and any RecallGap appended as its own '[lacuna]' line telling the model explicitly not to answer with what holds today — all inside one fence() with a per-render random nonce, so no recalled text can forge the closing delimiter and 'escape' into instruction-space.
recallPath.note: Only origin='inferred' is marked ('dedotto — non detto'); 'said' is left unlabelled on purpose, on the theory that a label appearing on every line stops being read (recall.ts:290-292). Same rule for the temporal label (recall.ts:731-748, temporalLabel): a live belief with no stated world time renders bare — the mark is the exception, not the default.

recallPath.what: The turn's taint is raised to the MAXIMUM trust_tier among everything just recalled, before the model is called — a fact a stranger planted months ago taints this turn exactly as if they had just spoken in it.

extraction.trigger: agent/loop.ts:624 (deps.onTurnEnd) -> agent/runtime.ts:490 -> core/memory/consolidator.ts:516-535 (Consolidator.notify): arms a 20s idle timer (CONSOLIDATION_IDLE_MS, consolidator.ts:87) after every turn, or fires immediately once 12 turns pass without a qualifying pause (CONSOLIDATION_CEILING, consolidator.ts:109). On fire, execute() (consolidator.ts:637) calls core/memory/ingest.ts:117 ingestPending(). Manual escape hatch: `muffin memory extract` (cli/memory.ts:175-237) drives the identical Consolidator.runNow() path so a hand-typed run cannot diverge from the automatic one.
extraction.model: the 'light lane' — config.models.light, wrapped by agent/providers/light-lane.ts and bound once in agent/runtime.ts:209-213 (billed under principal {kind:'system',source:'consolidation'}, ingest.ts:39-42). The SAME wrapped model instance is reused for extraction (extract.ts), the contradiction judge (judge.ts) and the LLM reranker (rerank.ts) — one lane, three consumers.
extraction.whatItProduces: ExtractedFact[] per episode — {subject, predicate, object, subjectKind, validFrom|null, confidence, matters/charged -> importance 0..2} (extract.ts:25-56) — each then reconciled in core/memory/ingest.ts:304-490 against the subject's current active facts for that predicate: no prior belief -> facts row inserted directly (no judge call, no cost); identical to the current belief -> skipped for free; otherwise -> judged and inserted alongside a coexist/supersede/temporal_scope/review outcome. Everything this pipeline produces has origin='said' by construction (extraction rule 2 forbids inference); 'inferred' is a declared-future producer (the 'observing spine', MVP #5) that does not exist yet.
extraction.versioning: core/memory/schema.ts:40 (episodes.extraction_v, default 0) checked against core/memory/schema.ts:217 (EXTRACTION_VERSION = 1). core/memory/store.ts:218-229 (pendingEpisodes) selects extraction_v < EXTRACTION_VERSION, oldest first. core/memory/store.ts:237-244 (markExtracted) advances it per-episode, called right after that single episode's extraction+judge calls finish (core/memory/ingest.ts:266) rather than at batch end, so a crash replays at most one episode. Bumping EXTRACTION_VERSION re-queues the entire corpus for replay; nothing currently does so (comment at schema.ts:217 states the intent, but there is no code path that increments it programmatically or a CLI verb that forces a full replay).

mechanisms.name: idle debounce (the flow)
mechanisms.trigger: re-armed on every turn for tenant 'host' only; fires 20s after the last turn, or immediately once 12 turns have accumulated without a 20s pause (measured on the owner's own 4-month corpus, not guessed).
mechanisms.cost: spends tokens — one light-model extraction call per non-skipped episode, plus one light-model judge call per predicate that already has a differing active belief.

mechanisms.name: backlog drain (flow, convergence)
mechanisms.file: core/memory/consolidator.ts:189 (CONSOLIDATION_DRAIN_MS = CONSOLIDATION_IDLE_MS), :717-723 (drainAgain gate: fetched>=limit AND marked>0)
mechanisms.trigger: self-continues at the same 20s cadence after any fire whose page was both full and made progress, until the backlog is exhausted; always yields to a live turn arriving mid-drain.
mechanisms.cost: spends tokens, but no more in total than the live lane would have paid anyway — same one extraction per episode, just paid earlier and denser instead of spread out.

mechanisms.name: duplicate sweep (the stock)
mechanisms.file: core/memory/maintenance.ts:132-177 (sweepDuplicates), gated at core/memory/consolidator.ts:678-697 (only when factsAdded>0)
mechanisms.trigger: runs synchronously at the end of every batch that added at least one fact; retires exact-normalised-string duplicate active beliefs for the same (subject,predicate,object), newest wins, deterministic so two racing processes pick the same survivor and need no lock.
mechanisms.cost: spends nothing — pure SQL over rows the batch just produced, no model call, no embedding, no network (maintenance.ts:21-25).

mechanisms.name: review register, read and answered (stock, human-driven)
mechanisms.file: core/memory/maintenance.ts:212-226 (openContradictions), :286-305 (resolveContradiction); cli/memory.ts:256-311 (muffin memory review), :323-343 (muffin memory review keep <fact-id>)
mechanisms.trigger: not scheduled at all — read on demand by the owner; 'open' is derived (both facts of the pair still active), not a stored status, so a question closes itself the moment the conversation supersedes either fact.
mechanisms.cost: spends nothing to read; answering costs one supersede() write and no model call — the owner decides, never the model (ADR-0032 §9 kept intact).

notBuilt.what: Dream / compaction — profiles and digests, the derived plane's summarization layer
notBuilt.why: missing the consumer, not the producer: writing a compactor would mean paying model calls to fill a table that no read path queries. 'Prima il lettore, poi lo scrittore' (reader first, writer second).
notBuilt.evidence: docs/blueprint/adr/0040-la-manutenzione-e-guidata-dai-dati.md:247-251 ('Le tabelle profiles e digests hanno zero scrittori e zero lettori'); confirmed at the code level — core/memory/schema.ts:151-167 declares both tables and repo-wide search finds no INSERT/SELECT against either outside schema.ts itself.

notBuilt.why: three independent, each-sufficient reasons: (1) no defensible decay rate exists in this corpus's research — the nearest number, LLM overconfidence of 15-27 points, is a constant calibration offset, not a time constant; (2) no reader — the only threshold on confidence anywhere is extract.ts:176 (>=0.4) applied once at write time, after that it is only ever displayed (`muffin memory why`); (3) decaying it would be a DELETE with extra steps — a belief that slides under a recall threshold becomes unrecoverable with no expired_at, no superseded_by, nothing `muffin memory why` can show, which is exactly what 'never delete a row' exists to prevent.

notBuilt.what: Expiry sweep (world-time closure on facts still believed true, plus entities.expired_at)
notBuilt.why: nothing to sweep yet: valid_to is written only by supersede() (called from judge verdicts and the duplicate sweep), never by addFact in the one production call site (reconcile). entities.expired_at has no writer at all. Building the sweep now would be a guard that can never fire.
notBuilt.evidence: docs/blueprint/adr/0040-la-manutenzione-e-guidata-dai-dati.md:237-245; cross-checked in code at core/memory/ingest.ts:323-345 (addFact call omits validTo) and core/memory/store.ts:38-56 (FactInput.validTo exists on the type but reconcile never sets it)

notBuilt.what: Predicate merge proposals (the second half of the predicate-vocabulary audit)
notBuilt.why: detection is built (the predicate_vocabulary invariant, warning-only, fires past 80 distinct predicates) but proposing an actual merge needs a synonymy judgment — either a model call (breaks ADR-0040's 'maintenance spends nothing' rule) or a hand-written synonym list (the closed vocabulary ADR-0032 already rejected once). Left open, in roadmap.
notBuilt.evidence: docs/blueprint/adr/0040-la-manutenzione-e-guidata-dai-dati.md:253-260; detection half at core/memory/invariants.ts:43,110-118 (PREDICATE_VOCABULARY_THRESHOLD=80, calibrated on the old system's 43-predicate/329-edge graph where 26 of 43 were used exactly once)

notBuilt.what: Cross-connector identity linking (the identities table's proposed -> confirmed flow)
notBuilt.why: the columns and states are built as structural foundation ('costano zero') but the actual linking flow is deliberately not built until a second remote connector exists to make cross-connector merging a real question — confirmation is required to go through an out-of-band channel (a code generated on one connector, entered on the other), never a same-channel 'yes that's me'.

notBuilt.what: `muffin run` headless does not consolidate live
notBuilt.why: the idle-debounce timer is deliberately `unref()`'d so a scriptable one-shot command exits immediately after answering instead of hanging around 20s to extract; episodes from a headless run stay pending by construction until the next long-lived process (gateway/REPL) drains them.
notBuilt.evidence: core/memory/consolidator.ts:576-580 (timer.unref comment); restated as a known, unfixed limitation in docs/blueprint/adr/0040-la-manutenzione-e-guidata-dai-dati.md:262-266

gaps.what: profiles and digests: zero writers AND zero readers, confirmed at the code level, not just declared in the ADR
gaps.evidence: core/memory/schema.ts:151-167 (declaration only); no match anywhere in core/, agent/, or cli/ (excluding schema.ts itself) for an INSERT into or SELECT from either table
gaps.why_it_matters: one of the architecture's three named planes ('evidence / graph / derived') is, in the running system, pure DDL — a third of the documented memory model does not exist as code. This is the exact 'declared and connected to nothing' pattern the codebase's own comments repeatedly flag by number (store.ts and consolidator.ts both reference it as a running count of prior incidents).

gaps.what: identities has zero production writers; episodes.actor_id and facts.speaker_id — the two foreign keys into it — are consequently always NULL in every live write path
gaps.evidence: no `INSERT INTO identities` outside core/memory/invariants.test.ts:117 (a test fixture); no production `addEpisode` call (agent/loop.ts:273, agent/loop.ts:529, core/vault/vault.ts:238, agent/observe-run.ts:105) ever passes actorId; the one production `addFact` call (core/memory/ingest.ts:324) never passes speakerId
gaps.why_it_matters: the ontology's headline claim for this table — 'one person seen from two connectors is two identities until someone confirms otherwise' — cannot be observed happening anywhere yet, and below the episode's own `role` column, the store has no notion of which specific speaker (in a group of several) said a given thing.

gaps.what: entities.summary and entities.expired_at: declared columns, zero writers
gaps.evidence: core/memory/store.ts:295-302 (upsertEntity's INSERT list is tenant_id, kind, name, recorded_at only — summary is absent); entities.expired_at confirmed unwritten in docs/blueprint/adr/0040-la-manutenzione-e-guidata-dai-dati.md:241
gaps.why_it_matters: an entity can never be marked retired/merged, and the one column that could hold a short human-readable gloss of who/what an entity is (useful exactly where `muffin memory why` or recall shows a bare name) is dead weight in the schema.

gaps.what: MemoryStore.isFunctional() has zero production call sites — the functional-predicate rule is enforced only offline, never at write time
gaps.evidence: grep across core/, agent/, cli/ for `.isFunctional(` matches only core/memory/store.test.ts:106-107 and core/memory/ingest.test.ts:363; core/memory/ingest.ts's reconcile() (lines 304-490) never calls it, despite a comment at ingest.ts:362 describing what it 'now means'. The only live consumer of functional_predicates is the direct SQL join inside the invariant check (core/memory/invariants.ts:110-118), run by `muffin memory check`, not by the ingest pipeline.
gaps.why_it_matters: the one predicate class the schema calls out as 'must never be a set' (date_of_birth, legal_name, tax_id, place_of_birth) can end up with two simultaneous active values if the judge ever mis-verdicts 'coexist' on one, and nothing refuses or even flags it at write time — only a manually-run, separate health check catches it after the fact.

gaps.what: a failed LLM rerank is mislabelled as a successful one in recall's own `strategies` field
gaps.evidence: core/memory/rerank.ts:64-92 (LlmReranker.rerank catches its own provider/parse failures and silently returns candidates.slice(0, topK) — the plain RRF order); core/memory/recall.ts:586-591 pushes the string `rerank(<id>)` onto `strategies` unconditionally once the branch (candidate count >= RERANK_MIN_CANDIDATES) is entered, with no way to observe that rerank() internally fell back
gaps.why_it_matters: RecallResult.strategies is documented as existing precisely so 'a degraded recall is never silent' (core/memory/recall.ts:266-267), and the vector half honors that (it appends `vector-non-disponibile(<error>)` on failure, recall.ts:503) — but the rerank half does not, so an unreachable reranker looks, from the one field the system exposes for this, identical to a reranker that worked.

gaps.what: surface/since/until on the vector half are a post-filter on the fetched k-NN candidates, not a partition inside the index — the same shape as the tenant-isolation bug this file already fixed once, one level down
gaps.evidence: core/memory/recall.ts:432-508: `deps.vectors.search(tenantId, query, limit*2)` fetches by tenant-partitioned similarity only, then surface/since/until/includeSuperseded are applied in application code afterwards. Contrast tenant scoping itself, which vectors.ts:43-50 moved INSIDE the vec0 partition key precisely because a post-filter let a busier tenant push another tenant's hits out of the k window entirely.
gaps.why_it_matters: on a corpus where most chunks are on one surface, a `surface` filter that excludes them can under-fill the k window before the requested `limit` is reached, silently returning fewer semantic matches than exist deeper in the true ranking — narrower than the FTS half, which applies the same filter inside SQL before any cap. Not a tenant leak (the partition key still holds) and not a mislabelling (an excluded hit never reaches the item list unmarked), so it did not meet the bar for a fix inside this slice; worth revisiting if `muffin doctor`/an eval ever shows recall thinning out under a surface filter.
